Common_Use: Provides temporary relief from mild fever, headache, and generalized body pain.
Precautions: Do not exceed maximum daily dose. Avoid alcohol consumption during use.
Side_Effects: Nausea, mild rash, rare liver toxicity with overdose.
Contraindications: Severe liver impairment or hypersensitivity to acetaminophen.
Warning: Discontinue use and consult a physician if fever lasts more than 3 days.

Common_Use: Helps clear nasal passages and reduce nasal congestion and sneezing.
Precautions: Use as directed on label. Avoid prolonged use beyond 5 days for decongestant sprays.
Side_Effects: Nasal dryness, mild stinging, rebound congestion if overused.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity to ingredients.
Warning: Consult a doctor if nasal congestion is accompanied by severe sinus pain.

Common_Use: Used to reduce body temperature during fever episodes and relieve associated body aches.
Precautions: Take with adequate water. Avoid combining with other paracetamol-containing products.
Side_Effects: Mild stomach discomfort, skin rash.
Contraindications: Severe hepatic failure.
Warning: Seek immediate medical evaluation if fever exceeds 102°F (38.9°C) or persists.

Common_Use: Helps relieve mild-to-moderate headache and localized muscle tension pain.
Precautions: Take with food or milk to minimize gastric discomfort. Hydrate well.
Side_Effects: Stomach upset, heartburn, mild dizziness.
Contraindications: Active peptic ulcer, severe kidney disease, third trimester pregnancy.
Warning: Avoid long-term continuous use without medical supervision.

Common_Use: Relieves flu-associated fever, body pain, and headache.
Precautions: Ensure proper rest and fluid intake alongside medication.
Side_Effects: Mild nausea, allergic skin reaction.
Contraindications: Known hypersensitivity or acute liver disorders.
Warning: Flu symptoms in high-risk individuals require direct medical consultation.

Common_Use: Neutralizes excess stomach acid to provide quick relief from heartburn and sour stomach.
Precautions: Do not take within 2 hours of other oral medications as it may affect absorption.
Side_Effects: Constipation or diarrhea depending on salt combination, intestinal cramps.
Contraindications: Severe renal impairment.
Warning: Consult a gastroenterologist if acid reflux occurs more than twice weekly.

Common_Use: Reduces stomach acid production for symptomatic heartburn relief.
Precautions: Swallow whole with water. Take 30 to 60 minutes before meals if needed.
Side_Effects: Headache, dizziness, mild constipation or diarrhea.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity to H2 blockers.
Warning: Do not use continuously for more than 14 days without consulting a doctor.

Common_Use: Replaces lost fluids and essential electrolytes caused by diarrhea or vomiting.
Precautions: Sip frequently in small quantities. Mix exact ratio specified on packet.
Side_Effects: Extremely rare when properly diluted; mild bloating if consumed too fast.
Contraindications: Severe intestinal obstruction or uncontrollable vomiting requiring IV fluids.
Warning: ORS is not an antibiotic. Seek emergency care if severe dehydration occurs.

Common_Use: Relieves sneezing, runny nose, watery eyes, and itching caused by allergies.
Precautions: May cause mild drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until response is known.
Side_Effects: Drowsiness, dry mouth, mild fatigue.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity to cetirizine or hydroxyzine, end-stage renal disease.
Warning: Avoid concurrent alcohol use.

Common_Use: Provides relief from allergic rhinitis symptoms including sneezing, itching, and runny nose.
Precautions: Take once daily or as directed on OTC product packaging.
Side_Effects: Headache, dry mouth, fatigue.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity to loratadine.
Warning: Consult a doctor if allergy symptoms do not improve after 7 days.

Common_Use: Reduces inflammation, joint stiffness, and muscle soreness after exertion.
Precautions: Take after meals. Drink plenty of water.
Side_Effects: Stomach discomfort, nausea, mild heartburn.
Contraindications: Active GI bleeding, aspirin-sensitive asthma, severe heart failure.
Warning: Stop taking if stomach pain or black tarry stools develop.

Common_Use: Provides temporary symptomatic relief for mild early-stage migraine headaches.
Precautions: Limit dietary caffeine intake while using this product.
Side_Effects: Restlessness, insomnia, mild tachycardia.
Contraindications: Uncontrolled hypertension, severe liver disease.
Warning: Frequent headaches require clinical neurological evaluation.

Common_Use: Soothes throat irritation, scratchiness, and painful swallowing.
Precautions: Allow lozenge to dissolve slowly in mouth. Do not chew.
Side_Effects: Mild tongue irritation, temporary altered taste sensation.
Contraindications: Children under 6 years unless advised by physician.
Warning: If sore throat is accompanied by high fever, consult a physician.

Common_Use: Adds bulk to stool to promote regular bowel movements and ease digestion.
Precautions: Consume with a full glass of water (at least 250 ml).
Side_Effects: Abdominal gas, bloating during initial days of use.
Contraindications: Difficulty swallowing, intestinal obstruction, acute abdominal pain.
Warning: Do not take immediately before bed.

Common_Use: Assists in regulating sleep-wake cycles for occasional sleeplessness.
Precautions: Take 30 minutes before bedtime. Do not drive after ingestion.
Side_Effects: Morning grogginess, vivid dreams, mild headache.
Contraindications: Autoimmune disorders, pregnancy, co-administration with sedatives.
Warning: Intended for short-term occasional use only.

Common_Use: Soothes skin itching, redness, and mild rash or insect bite irritation.
Precautions: For external application only. Do not apply on open wounds or eyes.
Side_Effects: Mild skin dryness, rare local irritation.
Contraindications: Known allergy to any lotion component.
Warning: Discontinue and seek care if skin rash spreads or shows signs of infection.

Common_Use: Temporarily suppresses dry, non-productive cough caused by minor throat irritation.
Precautions: Do not exceed recommended dose. Do not use for productive (mucus) cough.
Side_Effects: Drowsiness, dizziness, nausea.
Contraindications: Concurrent MAOI inhibitor therapy, severe asthma.
Warning: Consult a doctor if cough lasts more than 7 days.

Common_Use: Relieves bloating, pressure, and gas discomfort in the stomach and digestive tract.
Precautions: Take after meals and at bedtime if needed. Thoroughly chew tablets.
Side_Effects: Extremely low side effect profile; rare mild loose stools.
Contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to simethicone.
Warning: Seek medical evaluation if abdominal pain is severe or localized.

Common_Use: Prescription antihypertensives require individualized clinical evaluation.
Precautions: Requires regular blood pressure monitoring under medical care.
Side_Effects: N/A - Consult physician for specific medication profile.
Contraindications: N/A - Clinical decision required.
Warning: High blood pressure cannot be self-treated. Consult a qualified cardiologist or physician.

Common_Use: Prevents and relieves motion-induced nausea, vomiting, and dizziness.
Precautions: Take 30 to 60 minutes before starting travel. Causes marked drowsiness.
Side_Effects: Drowsiness, dry mouth, blurred vision.
Contraindications: Glaucoma, enlarged prostate, severe respiratory distress.
Warning: Avoid driving or operating machinery after consumption.

Common_Use: Provides localized relief for joint pain and stiffness in hands, knees, or ankles.
Precautions: Apply topically to clean skin. Wash hands after application. Do not cover with tight bandages.
Side_Effects: Local skin redness, dryness, mild itching.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity to NSAIDs, open wounds.
Warning: Avoid applying to damaged or broken skin.
